## Verified this step (measured, reproducible)

1. **The filed dominant hypothesis is implausible.** Autonomous sessions spawn
   with `permissionMode: bypassPermissions` (`spawn_session.py` L1970, L2388-94,
   L2597), so a genuine permission PROMPT is unreachable in the affected
   sessions. The observed "user doesn't want to proceed" rejection text is how
   a never-completed PreToolUse gate is recorded at session stop, not evidence
   of a dialog. The PreToolUse-hook path is the surviving mechanism: a
   PreToolUse hook runs BEFORE the tool launches, which is exactly why even
   the instant background "Async task launched" ack never arrived.

2. **PreToolUse guard-hook cost scales with argv size — measured.** Feeding the
   real Step 10d gate body (extracted verbatim from SKILL.md, 26,478 bytes /
   412 lines) to each of the 9 PreToolUse Bash hooks as PreToolUse JSON:

   | argv bytes | guard_repo_root_branch | guard_tmp_tmux_sweep | guard_root_code_commit |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | 22 (control) | 0.12s | 0.08s | 0.08s |
   | 3,587 | 1.48s | 1.34s | 1.31s |
   | 13,929 | 8.00s | 6.43s | 7.30s |
   | 26,478 (real gate) | 17.16s | 12.94s | 15.81s |
   | 52,957 | 42.42s | 27.81s | 30.39s |
   | 105,915 | 66.72s | 39.02s | 48.14s |

   The other 6 hooks stay under 0.1s at every size. Scaling is
   linear-to-mildly-superlinear. Mechanism: these guards (2,464 / 379 / 1,916
   lines) split the command into clauses, then fork `printf | grep -qE` pairs
   and awk char-scans PER CLAUSE — a 412-line body becomes hundreds of clauses
   x several process spawns each. At the real gate size that is ~17s (max
   single hook) to ~46s (sum) of pre-launch latency per dispatch.

3. **No hook carries a `timeout`** — re-verified across all 16 Pre/PostToolUse/
   Stop entries; only `SessionStart` has one (15s). So ANY hook stall is
   unbounded by construction. This is the load-bearing finding: it makes the
   wedge unbounded regardless of which stall mechanism dominates.

4. **Prong 1 is both NARROWER and DIFFERENT from the filing.** #2005 already
   landed the detached script-file gate shape, so "pin the gate to the detached
   shape" is done. The RESIDUAL is that the launcher still embeds the whole
   multi-KB body in the Bash argv via a `cat > "$LINT_GATE_SCRIPT" <<'EOF'`
   heredoc (SKILL.md L11812-11817; same at L13887-13893) — and guards scan the
   whole argv INCLUDING heredoc bodies. So the 26 KB still gets scanned even on
   the "fixed" shape. Composing the gate script with the WRITE tool instead of
   a Bash heredoc drops the argv to ~60 bytes and removes the cost at source.
   This is the rule CLAUDE.md ALREADY mandates for `post-marker --file`
   ("compose that file via the WRITE tool, never a Bash heredoc — the guard
   scans the whole Bash argv including heredoc bodies", #1756); the gate recipe
   simply never adopted it.

5. **Prong 3 unaddressed** — no watcher lane keys on a pending `tool_use` with
   no `tool_result`; the only `tool_result` reference is a delivered-prompt
   classifier helper (`autonomous_session_watch.py` L3263-3266).

## Refuted this step

**git index-lock blocking is NOT the unbounded factor.** `guard_root_code_commit.sh`
does make live git calls against the shared root per gated path (L1167-1202:
`diff --cached --name-only`, `ls-files -s`, `hash-object`), so a lock-contention
stall was the leading candidate. Control test in a throwaway repo with
`index.lock` held: all three READ ops returned in 0.00s (rc=0); only the WRITE
op failed, and it failed FAST (rc=128). Read ops do not take the index lock.
Branch closed.

## Residual gap (plan-time item, not a blocker)

Measured hook cost at the real gate size is tens of seconds; the observed
wedges were 1.2-2.4h. The duration is NOT reproduced. Surviving candidates:
(a) fork amplification under fleet load — these guards spawn hundreds of
processes each, and the VM runs ~15 concurrent sessions (cf. #2039's loadavg
~20 threshold, #2054's measured ~6x contention penalty); (b) an
input-dependent unbounded loop in a guard (`guard_tmp_tmux_sweep.sh` L90 has a
`while :;` parse loop). Prong 2 makes the residual moot rather than requiring
it to be solved: a bounded hook converts an unbounded wedge into a loud
failure. The plan should NOT block on reproducing the full duration.

## Prong re-ranking for the planner

1. **Hook timeouts** (was prong 2) — promote to FIRST. Smallest diff, bounds
   the failure class regardless of mechanism, independently valuable.
2. **Gate argv shape** (was prong 1, redirected) — compose gate scripts via
   Write, not a Bash heredoc; removes ~46s/dispatch and the scan surface.
   Drop or allowlist the `sudo -n choom` prelude is a SEPARATE, smaller item
   (denied anyway, FAIL-OPEN by design, and NOT the cost driver — measured).
3. **Watcher pending-call lane** (was prong 3) — keep last; it is the backstop
   that catches whatever 1+2 miss.

Advancing to `planning`. Assumption: the residual duration gap is a plan-time
investigation item, not a Step 1 blocker — prong 2 bounds the class without it.
